Protocol amendment before the reveal and before any measured run (stricter: it withholds more and weakens no claim, threshold or prediction). Amendment A1 adopts Q56, which replaces the per-finding withheld.jsonl rule: R2 now checks one bundle commitment per corpus entry, sealed target and Morph's new-law set (always), no committed per-law output, and no PROVED/REFUTED split in the summary outside a corpus detection. HUMAN_ANSWERS Q56, verbatim as relayed by the coordinator: brave-wright's disclosure rule is confirmed, with these amendments. The repo is public, so its Actions logs are public too. 1. The committed shape must not depend on whether there are findings. HOLON is deterministic and public, and the pins are public. So per-law verdicts, even only PROVED and UNKNOWN, reveal by omission which laws were refuted, and a withheld count or record points anyone at the pin. While a sealed target's embargo holds, commit only: (a) aggregates that never split PROVED from REFUTED: documents extracted, laws derived, decided (PROVED+REFUTED together) and UNKNOWN, per target and rule family; (b) one sha256 commitment per target over the canonical bundle of all its deterministic per-law outputs (laws, records, traces, witnesses). It is committed always, findings or not. Never commit a per-finding record, law id, class or withheld count. Every prediction whose outcome depends on refutations is recorded alike, as "withheld (embargo)" with a commitment. The adjudications stay in your session transcript, not in the bundle, so the bundle can be regenerated from the pinned tree. 2. Baselines too. Raw tool-output counts may be reported. Adjudicated detections on a sealed target follow rule 1. 3. Morph is deployed too. Verdicts already on the lead are unchanged. New laws' verdicts from your --roles run follow rule 1 until they are adjudicated and the human has decided. 4. The corpus exemption covers only findings matched to the entry's known, fixed defect. Any other refutation on a pre-fix commit follows rule 1. 5. Channels. No sealed-target analysis runs in CI. No plaintext goes in commits, commit messages, PR bodies, comments or CI output. The plaintext stays in your session, outside the repo. Alert brave-wright with only the target id and the bundle commitment. The human decides when each bundle opens. The adjudicator's class is advisory: nothing on a sealed target is published on its say-so. Your prereg's protocol should fix rule 1's aggregates and the bundle's canonical form (sorted paths, a sha256 per file, then a sha256 of that list).
